title: The Client Pitch
prompt: A potential client wants a proposal by tomorrow. Winning this deal would be huge, but the timeline is brutal.

leftChoice.label: Pull an all-nighter
leftChoice.outcomeText: The proposal is sharp. The client is impressed and you land the deal. You're running on fumes though.

rightChoice.label: Ask for a deadline extension
rightChoice.outcomeText: The client agrees to wait but mentions a competitor was faster. You feel the pressure.

title: The Travel Week
prompt: You're booked for client site visits Monday through Friday in another city. Your family has plans this weekend.

leftChoice.label: Fly back Friday night
leftChoice.outcomeText: You make it home exhausted but in time for weekend plans. Red-eye flights are rough.

rightChoice.label: Stay through the weekend
rightChoice.outcomeText: You bond with the client team over the weekend. Your family is disappointed.

title: The Scope Creep
prompt: The client keeps adding requirements outside the original scope. The team is already stretched thin.

leftChoice.label: Accommodate the requests
leftChoice.outcomeText: The client is delighted. Your team is burning out. The project margin is evaporating.

rightChoice.label: Push back with a change order
rightChoice.outcomeText: The client grumbles but signs the change order. Your firm's margin stays healthy.

title: The Utilization Target
prompt: Your utilization rate is at 70%. The firm expects 85%. There's a project available but it's mind-numbingly boring.

leftChoice.label: Take the boring project
leftChoice.outcomeText: Your utilization jumps. The partner is happy. You spend weeks doing repetitive analysis.

rightChoice.label: Hold out for something better
rightChoice.outcomeText: Your utilization stays low. The staffing team flags your name. But you're rested.

title: The Partner's Pet Project
prompt: A senior partner asks you to help with their pet initiative. It's not billable but could build a powerful relationship.

leftChoice.label: Help the partner
leftChoice.outcomeText: The partner remembers favors. You're now on their radar for top engagements.

rightChoice.label: Focus on billable work
rightChoice.outcomeText: Your utilization looks great. The partner barely remembers your name.

title: The Client Dinner
prompt: The client VP invites you to dinner after a long day on-site. You're exhausted and have an early flight tomorrow.

leftChoice.label: Go to dinner
leftChoice.outcomeText: Great conversation. The VP opens up about upcoming projects. You're dead tired the next day.

rightChoice.label: Politely decline
rightChoice.outcomeText: You get sleep. The VP doesn't mention it again, but seems slightly cooler tomorrow.

title: The Deliverable Crunch
prompt: The final deliverable is due Friday. It's Wednesday and the data analysis is only half done. The deck needs to be perfect.

leftChoice.label: Work through the night
leftChoice.outcomeText: You deliver a polished deck on time. The client loves it. You crash hard over the weekend.

rightChoice.label: Negotiate a Monday deadline
rightChoice.outcomeText: The client is annoyed but accepts. The extra time lets you produce better analysis.

title: The Knowledge Transfer
prompt: The engagement is ending. The client wants thorough documentation and training sessions, but you're already being staffed on a new project.

leftChoice.label: Do extensive handover
leftChoice.outcomeText: The client sings your praises. They specifically request you for future work.

rightChoice.label: Do a quick handover document
rightChoice.outcomeText: You start the new project on time. The client team struggles with the transition.

title: The Competing Client
prompt: A client asks you to share insights from a competitor's engagement. It would strengthen your relationship but crosses ethical lines.

leftChoice.label: Share general industry insights only
leftChoice.outcomeText: You thread the needle carefully. The client appreciates your integrity.

rightChoice.label: Decline entirely
rightChoice.outcomeText: The client is slightly frustrated but respects your professionalism.

title: The Internal Training
prompt: Your firm is running a week-long training program. Attending means being off a client project.

leftChoice.label: Attend the training
leftChoice.outcomeText: You learn new frameworks and network with colleagues. Your utilization takes a hit.

rightChoice.label: Stay on the client project
rightChoice.outcomeText: Your billable hours look great. You miss out on new skills and connections.

title: The Uncomfortable Finding
prompt: Your analysis reveals the client's strategy is fundamentally flawed. Telling them risks the relationship.

leftChoice.label: Present the hard truth
leftChoice.outcomeText: The room goes silent. After initial shock, the CEO says 'this is exactly why we hired you.'

rightChoice.label: Soften the message
rightChoice.outcomeText: The client nods along happily. The real problems persist but the engagement continues.

title: The Expense Report
prompt: You had a client dinner that was borderline personal. The expense policy is ambiguous.

leftChoice.label: Expense it
leftChoice.outcomeText: Finance flags the receipt. You get a gentle warning about expense guidelines.

rightChoice.label: Pay out of pocket
rightChoice.outcomeText: Your wallet is lighter but your conscience is clear.

title: The Team Staffing
prompt: You need to staff your project team. A junior analyst is available and cheap, but a senior would ensure quality.

leftChoice.label: Request the senior
leftChoice.outcomeText: The deliverable quality is top-notch. The project margin is thin.

rightChoice.label: Take the junior
rightChoice.outcomeText: You spend half your time coaching. The margins look great but you're stretched.

title: The Conference Circuit
prompt: An industry conference is next week. Great for networking and business development, but you're mid-engagement.

leftChoice.label: Attend the conference
leftChoice.outcomeText: You make great connections and generate two leads. Your project team covers for you.

rightChoice.label: Stay with the client
rightChoice.outcomeText: The client appreciates your dedication. You miss some valuable industry networking.

title: The Up-or-Out Pressure
prompt: Review season is approaching. You've been at the same level for two years. The unspoken expectation is clear: grow or leave.

leftChoice.label: Campaign aggressively for promotion
leftChoice.outcomeText: You take on extra responsibilities and visibility projects. The hours are brutal but you're noticed.

rightChoice.label: Focus on doing great work
rightChoice.outcomeText: Your work is solid. Senior leadership wonders if you have 'leadership ambition' though.

title: The Proposal Sprint
prompt: Your firm is bidding on a massive government contract. They need proposal support this weekend.

leftChoice.label: Join the proposal team
leftChoice.outcomeText: The proposal is submitted. If you win, you're first in line for the project team.

rightChoice.label: Decline - you need rest
rightChoice.outcomeText: You enjoy your weekend. The proposal team remembers who helped and who didn't.

title: The Client Presentation Mishap
prompt: Minutes before a major client presentation, you discover a critical error in the financial model. Fixing it takes 30 minutes.

leftChoice.label: Delay the presentation
leftChoice.outcomeText: The client is annoyed at the delay but appreciates the accurate numbers.

rightChoice.label: Present with a caveat
rightChoice.outcomeText: The client spots the caveat and questions your attention to detail. Awkward.

title: The Pro Bono Engagement
prompt: A nonprofit asks your firm for pro bono consulting. It's meaningful work but won't count toward your billable targets.

leftChoice.label: Volunteer to lead it
leftChoice.outcomeText: The work is deeply satisfying. Your utilization dips but your soul is recharged.

rightChoice.label: Pass on it
rightChoice.outcomeText: You stay focused on billable engagements. Someone else takes the rewarding work.

title: The Difficult Stakeholder
prompt: The client's VP of Operations undermines your recommendations in every meeting. Your project sponsor is silent.

leftChoice.label: Address it directly with the VP
leftChoice.outcomeText: A tense but respectful conversation. The VP explains their concerns and you find common ground.

rightChoice.label: Escalate to your firm's partner
rightChoice.outcomeText: The partner makes a call. The VP backs off but resents the move.

title: The Bench Period
prompt: You're between engagements with no immediate project. The firm has internal initiatives, or you could use the downtime.

leftChoice.label: Drive an internal initiative
leftChoice.outcomeText: You build a useful framework the firm adopts. Partners notice your initiative.

rightChoice.label: Take some personal time
rightChoice.outcomeText: You recharge completely. HR notes your low initiative during bench time.

title: The Data Room Deep Dive
prompt: Due diligence for an M&A engagement starts tomorrow. Thousands of documents to review in a week.

leftChoice.label: Dive in with full intensity
leftChoice.outcomeText: You surface critical findings. The partner calls your work 'exceptional.' You haven't seen sunlight in days.

rightChoice.label: Set sustainable daily limits
rightChoice.outcomeText: You maintain sanity but miss some details. The team fills in the gaps.

title: The Client's Bad Idea
prompt: The client CEO is enthusiastic about an initiative that your analysis shows will fail. They expect your endorsement.

leftChoice.label: Diplomatically redirect
leftChoice.outcomeText: You present alternative approaches backed by data. The CEO is reluctant but listens.

rightChoice.label: Support and optimize
rightChoice.outcomeText: The project moves forward. When it struggles later, everyone remembers you supported it.

title: The Poached Colleague
prompt: A top analyst on your team just got poached by the client. You're mid-deliverable.

leftChoice.label: Absorb the workload yourself
leftChoice.outcomeText: You hold the project together single-handedly. The partner is grateful. You're burned out.

rightChoice.label: Request a replacement immediately
rightChoice.outcomeText: The replacement takes time to ramp up. There's a temporary dip in quality.

title: The Airport Lounge Networking
prompt: Waiting at the airport, you spot a potential client executive. You could network or enjoy your quiet time.

leftChoice.label: Introduce yourself
leftChoice.outcomeText: Great conversation! They mention an upcoming RFP. You pass the lead to your partner.

rightChoice.label: Enjoy the peace and quiet
rightChoice.outcomeText: You read your book and decompress. The opportunity passes unnoticed.

title: The Slide Deck Perfectionism
prompt: Your deck is 'good enough' but not perfect. The client meeting is in 2 hours. You could polish it or prep for Q&A.

leftChoice.label: Polish the slides
leftChoice.outcomeText: The deck looks stunning. The partner nods approvingly. You stumble on one unexpected question though.

rightChoice.label: Prep for the Q&A
rightChoice.outcomeText: The slides are fine. Your answers are razor sharp. The client is more impressed by your insights.

title: The Client Offsite Invitation
prompt: The client invites your team to their annual strategy offsite at a resort. It's a 3-day commitment.

leftChoice.label: Attend the full offsite
leftChoice.outcomeText: You build deep relationships with the client's leadership. Extended engagement is almost certain.

rightChoice.label: Send a junior in your place
rightChoice.outcomeText: The junior does fine but lacks the context to make the most of the networking.

title: The Methodology Debate
prompt: Your firm pushes a proprietary methodology, but you know an open-source approach would work better for this client.

leftChoice.label: Recommend the better approach
leftChoice.outcomeText: The client gets better results. Your firm's leadership questions your 'brand loyalty.'

rightChoice.label: Use the firm's methodology
rightChoice.outcomeText: It works okay. The client senses it wasn't the optimal path.

title: The Friday Night Email
prompt: It's 9 PM Friday. The client sends a 'quick question' that requires 2 hours of analysis. Monday is a holiday.

leftChoice.label: Answer tonight
leftChoice.outcomeText: The client is stunned by your responsiveness. Your weekend plans are shot.

rightChoice.label: Reply Tuesday morning
rightChoice.outcomeText: You enjoy the long weekend guilt-free. The client is mildly annoyed.

title: The Thought Leadership Piece
prompt: Your firm's marketing team wants you to write an article for the company blog. Good visibility but unbillable hours.

leftChoice.label: Write the article
leftChoice.outcomeText: The article goes viral in your industry. Several inbound leads follow. Partners are impressed.

rightChoice.label: Decline - too busy
rightChoice.outcomeText: Marketing asks someone else. You stay focused on client work.

title: The Junior's Mistake
prompt: A junior team member sent an unfinished analysis to the client. The client is confused and your partner is furious.

leftChoice.label: Take responsibility
leftChoice.outcomeText: You fix the situation and coach the junior. The partner appreciates your leadership.

rightChoice.label: Let the junior explain
rightChoice.outcomeText: The junior struggles. The client questions your team's quality control.

title: The Competitive Intelligence
prompt: A colleague from a competitor approaches you at a conference to 'share notes' about the industry.

leftChoice.label: Have a careful conversation
leftChoice.outcomeText: You learn some useful market intel while sharing nothing proprietary.

rightChoice.label: Keep your distance
rightChoice.outcomeText: You avoid any appearance of impropriety. Your compliance team would be proud.

title: The Implementation Gap
prompt: Your strategy recommendations are solid, but the client lacks the capability to execute. They want implementation support.

leftChoice.label: Propose an implementation phase
leftChoice.outcomeText: The engagement extends by 6 months. Your partner is thrilled. Your calendar weeps.

rightChoice.label: Recommend they build internal capacity
rightChoice.outcomeText: The client appreciates the honest advice. Your firm loses potential revenue.

title: The Multiple Client Juggle
prompt: You're staffed on two engagements simultaneously. Both client managers want you at their site on Tuesday.

leftChoice.label: Split the day between sites
leftChoice.outcomeText: You show face at both. The commute is exhausting and neither client gets your full attention.

rightChoice.label: Prioritize the bigger engagement
rightChoice.outcomeText: The smaller client feels deprioritized. The bigger client is satisfied.

title: The Excel Model From Hell
prompt: The inherited financial model has circular references, unlabeled tabs, and no documentation. You need results by Thursday.

leftChoice.label: Rebuild from scratch
leftChoice.outcomeText: The new model is clean and auditable. You work until 3 AM but the client is impressed.

rightChoice.label: Fix the critical errors only
rightChoice.outcomeText: The output is good enough. The model remains a ticking time bomb for whoever touches it next.

title: The Client's Christmas Party
prompt: The client invites your team to their holiday party. It's on a night you promised to take your family out.

leftChoice.label: Attend the party
leftChoice.outcomeText: You strengthen client bonds. Your family celebrates without you.

rightChoice.label: Keep the family commitment
rightChoice.outcomeText: Family night is wonderful. The client party goes on without you.

title: The RFP Response
prompt: An RFP just dropped and the response window is 10 days. It's a dream engagement but the proposal effort is massive.

leftChoice.label: Lead the proposal team
leftChoice.outcomeText: You produce a compelling proposal. Win or lose, leadership knows you stepped up.

rightChoice.label: Contribute sections only
rightChoice.outcomeText: You help without overcommitting. Someone else gets the proposal lead credit.

title: The Client Team Conflict
prompt: Two client directors disagree on priorities and both want your team to support their agenda.

leftChoice.label: Facilitate a resolution
leftChoice.outcomeText: You broker a compromise. Both directors grudgingly agree. Your partner says 'that's why we get paid well.'

rightChoice.label: Escalate to the project sponsor
rightChoice.outcomeText: The sponsor makes the call. You avoid the political minefield.

title: The Hotel Loyalty Dilemma
prompt: The firm's preferred hotel chain is cheaper but far from the client site. A nearby boutique hotel would save you commute time.

leftChoice.label: Stay at the nearby hotel
leftChoice.outcomeText: You sleep better and arrive fresh. Finance raises an eyebrow at the receipt.

rightChoice.label: Follow firm policy
rightChoice.outcomeText: You spend 45 minutes each way in traffic. At least your loyalty points are stacking up.

title: The Workshop Facilitator
prompt: The client wants a full-day strategy workshop. Facilitating it would showcase your skills but requires significant prep.

leftChoice.label: Facilitate the workshop
leftChoice.outcomeText: The workshop is a hit. The client CEO pulls you aside to say it was 'the best session in years.'

rightChoice.label: Suggest an external facilitator
rightChoice.outcomeText: The external facilitator does a decent job. You focus on the actual deliverables.

title: The Late-Night Flight Cancel
prompt: Your Friday night flight home is cancelled. Next available is Saturday afternoon.

leftChoice.label: Rent a car and drive
leftChoice.outcomeText: You arrive home at 2 AM, exhausted but at least you're home for the weekend.

rightChoice.label: Stay another night
rightChoice.outcomeText: You get some rest and fly home Saturday. Half the weekend is gone.

title: The Cross-Selling Opportunity
prompt: During your engagement, you discover the client also needs help with cybersecurity — your firm's other practice area.

leftChoice.label: Introduce the cybersecurity team
leftChoice.outcomeText: The cross-sell is successful. You earn internal referral credit and the client appreciates the full-service approach.

rightChoice.label: Stay in your lane
rightChoice.outcomeText: The client hires a competitor for cybersecurity. Your partner later asks 'why didn't you mention us?'

title: The Work-From-Home Request
prompt: The client expects consultants on-site 4 days a week. You want to work from home one extra day for personal reasons.

leftChoice.label: Request the extra WFH day
leftChoice.outcomeText: The client agrees reluctantly. Some team members follow suit, diluting the 'consultant presence.'

rightChoice.label: Show up as expected
rightChoice.outcomeText: The client values your commitment. The commute continues to wear you down.

title: The Mentor's Advice
prompt: Your mentor at the firm suggests you specialize in a niche area. It would narrow your options but deepen your expertise.

leftChoice.label: Specialize
leftChoice.outcomeText: You become the go-to expert. Clients request you by name. Your options narrow but your value increases.

rightChoice.label: Stay a generalist
rightChoice.outcomeText: You stay flexible and get varied projects. No one thinks of you first for anything specific.

title: The Sick on a Client Site
prompt: You wake up at the hotel feeling terrible. The client has a big meeting today that you're supposed to lead.

leftChoice.label: Push through the meeting
leftChoice.outcomeText: You deliver the meeting but everyone notices you look awful. Your recovery takes longer.

rightChoice.label: Have a colleague cover
rightChoice.outcomeText: Your colleague handles it well. You rest and recover by the next day.

title: The Client's IT Nightmare
prompt: The client's systems are ancient. You could build a workaround or recommend a full tech upgrade that extends the engagement.

leftChoice.label: Recommend the full upgrade
leftChoice.outcomeText: The client approves a 6-month technology transformation. Your utilization is secured for months.

rightChoice.label: Build the quick workaround
rightChoice.outcomeText: The workaround holds for now. The client appreciates the practical approach.

title: The Performance Review Feedback
prompt: Your annual review feedback says 'technically strong but needs to develop client relationships.' Building relationships means more travel.

leftChoice.label: Double down on client engagement
leftChoice.outcomeText: You attend every client event and dinner. Your relationships improve. Your personal life suffers.

rightChoice.label: Build relationships your own way
rightChoice.outcomeText: You find a balance that works for you. Progress is slower but sustainable.

title: The Client Data Breach
prompt: You discover a potential data breach at the client during your engagement. Reporting it could derail the project.

leftChoice.label: Report immediately
leftChoice.outcomeText: The project pauses for 2 weeks. The client is grateful you caught it before regulators did.

rightChoice.label: Note it for the final report
rightChoice.outcomeText: The breach expands. When it's discovered, people ask why you didn't flag it sooner.

title: The Rainmaking Dinner
prompt: A partner invites you to a business development dinner with a prospective Fortune 500 client. It's your anniversary.

leftChoice.label: Attend the dinner
leftChoice.outcomeText: The prospect is impressed. The partner recommends you for the engagement. Your partner at home is not impressed.

rightChoice.label: Keep your anniversary plans
rightChoice.outcomeText: A wonderful evening. The partner takes someone else and they build the relationship instead.

title: The Offshore Team Challenge
prompt: Budget constraints mean your analysis team is mostly offshore. Time zone differences are creating delays.

leftChoice.label: Overlap hours with early/late calls
leftChoice.outcomeText: The team syncs up well. Your 6 AM calls and 11 PM reviews are taking a toll.

rightChoice.label: Set strict handoff protocols
rightChoice.outcomeText: The async process works okay. There are occasional miscommunications that slow things down.

title: The Exit Interview Dilemma
prompt: A close colleague is leaving the firm. They ask if you're also considering leaving. You've been thinking about it.

leftChoice.label: Be honest about your doubts
leftChoice.outcomeText: Word gets around that you might be 'looking.' Leadership starts paying more attention to your engagement.

rightChoice.label: Keep your cards close
rightChoice.outcomeText: You maintain discretion. Your colleague leaves and you process your feelings alone.
